caption: The drawing is done in black ink on a light beige background and depicts an ornate iron railing or balustrade in front of a window with closed shutters. The railing features a repeating pattern of vertical twisted columns, each topped with decorative, leaf-like finials and flanked by similarly ornate, pointed elements. The upper part of the railing consists of a series of semicircular arches adorned with floral motifs and dots, each arch resting atop the vertical columns and continuing the decorative theme. The base of the ironwork is formed by intertwined, looping bands, and rests on a horizontally-lined surface that resembles wood grain. In the background, behind the railing, there are two large rectangular window shutters with horizontal slats, evenly divided down the center. On the right side of the drawing, there is a vertical double-headed arrow with the dimension "34" written beside it to indicate height. The lines of the drawing are consistent and detailed, and the composition is symmetrical, with all features regularly spaced. The overall color is monochromatic, consisting only of shades of black and grey ink on the paper.
title: Cast Iron Balcony Rail
